text.p: Russia raised 2.0 billion German marks ($1.2 billion) Thursday in its second international bond issue, which was well-received by investors.
"There has been a very good reception of the Russia Eurobond," an official at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said.

Credit Suisse First Boston and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell underwrote the seven-year bond, which was priced to yield 3.70 percentage points over German government bonds and will pay an annual interest rate of 9 percent.

The Russian bond issue came against a background of soft market conditions, with demand for high-yielding bonds weaker due to sharp price falls triggered by worries of a U.S. interest rate rise, bankers said.
However, they added that the rarity value of Russian debt boosted demand for the issue.
The bond issue followed Russia's successful $1.0 billion five-year deal in November, its first foreign bond since the 1917 revolution.
